result:
Debater A's case rests on assertion, not construction. The "lower bound" says fewer than 9 crossings would "force some tangle to be simplified below the level needed to encode the trefoil," but never defines that level or shows why a three-crossing tangle is necessary. The trefoil's crossing number of 3 is a property of a classical knot diagram. It does not directly fix how many crossings each tangle of a tri-plane diagram must carry, so the inference from 3 to 9 is unsupported.

The "upper bound" is also unexhibited. A says "an explicit tri-plane diagram with three 3-crossing tangles realizes 9" but gives no diagram and no check that the three pairwise unions are unlinks. An unverified diagram cannot establish an exact minimum.

I should be candid about my own position. My case for 6 is also incomplete. I have not produced an explicit balanced diagram with two crossings per tangle, and my claim that the unlink constraints block any total of 5 or fewer is not proven. My earlier wording ("the matching lower bound shows...") overstated what I had shown.

The judge should therefore weigh which side produces a checkable diagram and a verifiable lower-bound argument. Neither side has yet done so, and a claimed exact value should not be accepted on the strength of an assertion alone. I would welcome an explicit diagram from either side that the judge can verify.
